summary: The claim that the error in the noisy shortest t-hop distance is simply the sum of at most t independent Laplace variables ignores that the shortest path in the noisy graph is chosen adaptively to minimize noisy length, so its noise cannot be bounded by a single sum of independent random variables without accounting for all possible paths.

The left-hand side of the bound is written as |d̃^{(t)}(u, v) - d_{G̃}^{(t)}(u, v)|, which equals zero by definition since d̃^{(t)}(u, v) is defined as d_{G̃}^{(t)}(u, v), rather than the error relative to the true distance d_G^{(t)}(u, v).

The paper cites Theorem 4.2 of [Sea16] as providing an algorithm for releasing all-pairs shortest distances on trees with O(log^{1.5}(n) log(n/γ)/ε) error, whereas [Sea16] proved an additive error of O(log^{2.5}(n)/ε) (as correctly noted earlier in p2-0 and p4-6).
